sections.heading: Why nearly every freestanding sign in Pflugerville is a monument
sections.body:
Pflugerville's sign code is simple on one point. Unless the chapter says otherwise, every permanent freestanding sign must be a monument sign. For businesses in the city's public, commercial, and industrial zoning districts, the monument is the only permanent freestanding sign type the code lists.

The code also sets a masonry rule. A monument must be built into a masonry structure equal to at least 50 percent of the sign face area. The masonry can be no more than 150 percent of the sign face area. Other materials are allowed, as long as the masonry share is met and the colors fit the overall project.

In those commercial districts, a monument sign can be up to 8 feet tall and 72 square feet. You get one per lot for each street frontage. That is the same limit in every commercial and industrial district.

This matters if you are used to other cities. A tall pole or pylon sign for a single business is not part of Pflugerville's permitted sign list for commercial districts. Your roadside presence comes from a well-built monument and strong building signs.

Downtown has its own rules. The Downtown District Overlay has four subdistricts: Downtown Core, Pfluger Tract, South Downtown, and Western Gateway. In the Downtown Core, monument and low-profile pole signs are discouraged and allowed only under limited conditions. Elsewhere in the overlay, the Building Official can allow a low-profile pole sign in place of a monument where the code permits it.

We design Pflugerville monuments around the masonry rule from the start. We choose stone or brick that matches your building, size the sign face to the code, and plan the lighting.

sections.heading: What does the SH 130 and SH 45 corridor mean for your sign?
sections.body:
State Highway 130 and State Highway 45 opened in November 2006 as the first parts of Central Texas's tollway system. They made Pflugerville much easier to reach from across the region.

Stone Hill Town Center sits at the southwest corner of SH 130 and SH 45. The city's economic development site lists it with about 1 million square feet of retail space. Pecan Street (FM 1825) is another main route through the city. Pflugerville counted 65,191 residents at the 2020 census.

The corridor gets one special allowance in the sign code. A non-residential subdivision entrance sign on the SH 130 or SH 45 frontage road can be up to 25 feet tall and 200 square feet. On an arterial street, the limit is 10 feet and 100 square feet. These signs identify a whole development, not a single business.

Entrance signs come with conditions. They must be monument or pylon signs built of stone, brick, or other maintenance-free masonry. Electronic message centers are not allowed on them. They need an irrigated, landscaped area twice the size of the sign face. They must also sit at least 1,000 feet from another such sign or an existing billboard.

Every subdivision entrance sign needs an approved Master Signage Plan. An approved plan expires after two years if no progress is made on the project.

If you own or develop property along the corridor, we can design the entrance sign and help prepare the plan. If you are a tenant, we design your monument panel and building signs to work alongside it.

sections.heading: Pflugerville sign permits: Chapter 154 and the Building Official
sections.body:
Pflugerville's sign rules are in Chapter 154 of the city's Code of Ordinances. The Building Official reviews all sign permits and Master Signage Plans. Applications go through the city's online permit portal, and the Building Inspections department publishes the permanent sign application.

The code sets a clear review window. Within 10 business days of a complete application, the Building Official must either issue the permit or reject it. A rejection must name the code sections the sign does not meet.

A permit application must include detailed drawings showing the sign's size, design, structure, and location. Freestanding signs also need a plot plan showing buildings, parking, driveways, landscaping, and every existing and proposed sign on the lot. The drawings must show the proposed lighting and its levels. They must also show that the sign meets the National Electrical Code.

Structural review is part of the process. Sign plans must be certified by a qualified structural engineer for structural and wind load standards. Standard drawings prepared by an engineer are another accepted path.

The permanent sign application asks for the property owner's written consent. For an internally lit sign, it also asks for a master sign electrician's license number or an electrical sign contractor's license number. The form marks this as required to pull the permit.

The city inspects the lot during the sixth month after a permit is issued, or sooner if the owner asks. If construction is not substantially complete by then, the permit lapses and becomes void.

HSC checks Pflugerville's rules for your property before design. We then prepare the permit package, including drawings, the plot plan, and the engineering. We also confirm any contractor or license steps with Building Inspections. The city makes the final decision on each permit.

sections.heading: How big can your storefront sign be in Pflugerville?
sections.body:
Pflugerville sizes wall signs as a share of the building face, not by a flat number. In the General Business 1 district, a wall sign can cover up to 10 percent of the facade it sits on. The limit is 15 percent in the Public Facilities and Office districts. It is 5 percent in the light and general industrial districts.

There is also a cap on all signs on the lot combined. In General Business 1, the total can be 800 square feet, 10 percent of the main building's ground floor area, or 6 square feet per foot of street frontage. You get whichever of the three is greatest. Other districts use smaller numbers.

For a storefront, that usually means channel letters or a shaped logo sized to your facade. The way Pflugerville measures signs favors individual letters. Letters mounted on a plain wall are measured as the smallest rectangles around each word and graphic. A lit cabinet counts its whole lit face. We fabricate and wire the letters in our Houston shop, and our team mounts them.

Awnings and canopies need a sign permit in most commercial districts. The code has one firm rule for them. It bans internally illuminated fabric awning signs. If you want a lit sign over your door, a rigid metal canopy with channel letters is often the better path.

HSC builds commercial awnings and canopies in-house. That lets us plan the canopy, its sign, and the lighting as one design. We then check the whole package against your district's wall sign percentage before it goes to the city.

sections.heading: Refurbishing older signs and working with HSC in Pflugerville
sections.body:
Not every project needs a new sign. Pflugerville's permanent sign application includes a box for major maintenance to an existing sign. That tells you the city expects a permit for bigger repair work, not just new signs.

We repair and refurbish signs that have faded faces, failed lighting, loose letters, or worn finishes. On an older monument, we can often replace the faces and lighting and keep the masonry base. We check first whether the sign still meets the current code, because that affects what the city allows.

Every project, new or repair, follows the same steps.

First, we call you to understand your business and your site and to confirm the project is a good fit.

Second, our Austin-area staff do an on-site survey. We take exact measurements, check your frontage and facade, and look at power for lit signs.

Third, we deliver a free design mockup with an itemized estimate. The mockup shows the sign on your building or lot, sized to Pflugerville's limits.

Fourth, we prepare the permit package and track the city's review.

Fifth, we build the sign in our own Houston shop. Our work is UL-certified.

Sixth, our team installs the sign.

Every sign carries a 5-year warranty. If something fails under warranty, you call the same team that built it.

We work with businesses across Pflugerville, from Stone Hill Town Center and the SH 130 corridor to Pecan Street and the downtown overlay.

faqs.q: Can I put a pole or pylon sign in Pflugerville?
faqs.a: For a single business in a commercial district, generally no. Pflugerville's code requires permanent freestanding signs to be monument signs unless the chapter permits otherwise. The main exceptions are subdivision entrance signs for whole developments, which can be masonry pylons, and low-profile pole signs in parts of the downtown overlay. We design strong masonry monuments that work within these limits.

faqs.q: How tall can a monument sign be in Pflugerville?
faqs.a: In the public, commercial, and industrial zoning districts, a monument sign can be up to 8 feet tall and 72 square feet. You can have one per lot for each street frontage. The sign must sit in a masonry structure equal to at least half of the sign face area. Subdivision entrance signs on the SH 130 or SH 45 frontage roads have higher limits.

faqs.q: How long does Pflugerville take to review a sign permit?
faqs.a: The code says the Building Official will issue or reject a sign permit within 10 business days of receiving a complete application. A rejection must list the code sections the sign does not meet. The key word is complete. We prepare the drawings, plot plan, lighting details, and engineering up front so the application is ready for review.

faqs.q: Can my Pflugerville monument include a digital message sign?
faqs.a: Sometimes. Pflugerville allows electronic message centers for on-premises use only along streets its Master Transportation Plan lists as arterial or collector streets. They are not allowed on subdivision entrance signs. The zoning district matters too, since the code does not permit them in every district. We check your street type and zoning before we design a monument with a digital display.
